chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mihran, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement

He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is none from a servant who prevents anything from the Zakat of his wealth except that Allah, on the Day of Judgement, would Make that to be a serpent of Fire in his neck, eroding his flesh, until he is free from the Reckoning; and these are the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What they were niggardly with, from the Zakat.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth withheld from Zakat on the Day of Judgement according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse 'They will have applied to their necks that which they squandered' by specifying that the 'squandered' wealth refers specifically to Zakat. He describes the withheld amount transforming into a fiery serpent that encircles the neck and gnaws the flesh until the Reckoning is complete, emphasizing a literal and proportional manifestation of the withheld dues. This interpretation underscores the severity of neglecting obligatory alms in Shia jurisprudence, linking the specific quantity withheld to the physical punishment.
